title: From Accra to Seattle (with a Few Detours)
summary: How managing a print shop in Ghana taught me systems thinking—and why it matters at Salesforce.

content.html:
The Unlikely Tech Education

My first 'production environment' wasn't a server cluster—it was a 10x12 foot print shop in Accra's Makola market. Juggling toner refills, client demands, and a temperamental Heidelberg machine taught me:

  • User Experience: 'The client wants blue, not cyan' translates directly to UI design.
  • Debugging: When the printer jammed, I learned to trace problems upstream (literally—paper path analysis).

The Pivot Points

  1. 2009: Taught myself PHP with a dog-eared 'For Dummies' book and XAMPP.
  2. 2014: Built a church management system that crashed spectacularly during Easter service (my first 'postmortem').
  3. 2022: Shipped a Tableau integration at Salesforce that now processes 2M+ marketing events daily.
"In tech, your past isn't irrelevant—it's your secret advantage. My print shop days made me obsessive about observability."

Lessons for Career Changers

SkillPrint ShopSoftware Engineering
ResourcefulnessMacGyvered paper jamsDebugging legacy Perl at 2AM
Stakeholder MgmtNegotiating with ink suppliersAligning PMs and engineers

Lessons & Reflections

This part of the journey often gets overlooked. Behind every tool and framework lies a deeper story about perseverance, curiosity, and sometimes brute-force Googling. I remember the nights spent tweaking configurations, the moments of joy when something just worked, and the quiet satisfaction of solving problems no one else wanted to touch. These are the unsung victories that make our careers richer.

title: The Time I Almost Quit Tech (And Why I’m Glad I Didn’t)
summary: How hitting rock bottom became my career catalyst—and what I tell engineers on the brink.

content.html:
The Breaking Point

February 2018: I was:

  • Debugging a Laravel app for a client who vanished after delivery
  • Burning through savings with 3 months' rent due
  • Facing this error for the 11th hour straight:
    SQLSTATE[HY000] [2002] Connection refused

What Saved Me

  1. The Pivot: Switched from freelancing to contract work with guaranteed pay
  2. The Mentor: Met a senior dev who taught me:
    "Your value isn't in never failing—it's in how you recover."
  3. The Win: Landed a Shopify dev role by showcasing my failed project's postmortem

If You're Considering Quitting

Burnout3-day breakTook a literal hike (Forest Park, Portland)
Skill GapsTargeted learning30 mins daily on Laracasts

title: My Local Dev Setup: How I Stopped Fighting Docker and Made Peace
summary: From Docker disasters to harmonious containers—a survival guide for full-stack developers.

content.html:
The War of the Ports

When Docker (port 80) declared war on Laravel Valet (also port 80), my development environment became a battlefield. Key casualties:

  • Project A: Laravel app refusing to connect to MySQL
  • Project B: WordPress site showing 'Error establishing database connection'
  • My Sanity: Lost in docker-compose logs output

The Peace Treaty

# docker-compose.yml - The Armistice Agreement
version: '3.8'
services:
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "${APP_PORT:-8080}:80"  # Compromise: No more port 80 greed
    networks:
      - sail
    volumes:
      - '.:/var/www/html'
networks:
  sail:
    driver: bridge

Current Stack Allocation

ToolUse CaseWhen to Avoid
DockerMicroservices, team projectsQuick PHP script tests
ValetLegacy projects, local WordPressWhen you need containerization
"The best tool is the one you'll actually use. My setup now looks chaotic but works like a Swiss watch—if Swiss watches occasionally needed docker system prune."

title: The 3 Rules I Follow in Code Reviews (and Life)
summary: How giving feedback at Salesforce taught me more about people than programming.

content.html:
Rule #1: Assume Good Intent (Until Proven Otherwise)

At Salesforce, I reviewed a PR where a junior engineer committed node_modules. Instead of "WTF?", I wrote:

"Might want to add node_modules to .gitignore! 
Here's how our team handles dependencies: [link to docs]"

Result: They later told me this kept them from quitting tech.

The Framework

SituationBad ResponseBetter Approach
Messy code"This is unreadable""Could we break this into smaller functions?"
Buggy logic"This won't work""What edge cases should we consider?"
"A code review is a conversation, not a court ruling. The best feedback I've given started with 'What if...' instead of 'Don't...'"
